beats.narration: Begin by framing Course Foundations & Scope as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. This accelerated course covers material from the first-year sequence of courses and provides the foundation for all subsequent Computer Science courses. Consider this worked case: Students will use this course to prepare for advanced topics like algorithms, data structures, and software engineering. On screen, display a course roadmap graphic showing CSCI-140 as the central hub connecting to advanced CS courses. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.
beats.title: Course Foundations & Scope
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a course roadmap graphic showing CSCI-140 as the central hub connecting to advanced CS courses.

beats.narration: Now define Static vs. Dynamic Data Types precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Topics include tree and graph structures, nested data structures, objects, classes, inheritance, interfaces, object-oriented collection class libraries for abstract data types (for example stacks, queues, maps, and trees), and static versus dynamic data types. Consider this worked case: In statically typed languages, variable types are checked at compile time, whereas dynamically typed languages check types at runtime. On screen, show a side-by-side comparison table of static vs. dynamic typing with code snippets highlighting compile-time vs. runtime type resolution. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
beats.title: Static vs. Dynamic Data Types
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a side-by-side comparison table of static vs. dynamic typing with code snippets highlighting compile-time vs. runtime type resolution.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Object-Oriented Design Foundations operates in a concrete sequence. Software qualities related to object orientation, namely cohesion, minimal coupling, modifiability, and extensibility, are all introduced in this course, as well as a few elementary object-oriented design patterns. Consider this worked case: A parent class defines shared behavior, while child classes inherit and extend that behavior through polymorphism. On screen, render a class diagram illustrating inheritance relationships between a base class and derived classes. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.
beats.title: Object-Oriented Design Foundations
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Render a class diagram illustrating inheritance relationships between a base class and derived classes.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Abstract Data Types & Collections and make the decision criteria explicit. The Python language reference specifies lexical analysis, data model behavior, execution, expressions, statements, functions, classes, exceptions, and module import semantics. Consider this worked case: A stack implements last-in-first-out behavior, while a queue implements first-in-first-out behavior for ordered data processing. On screen, animate a stack and queue data structure showing push/pop and enqueue/dequeue operations with labeled elements. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
beats.title: Abstract Data Types & Collections
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Animate a stack and queue data structure showing push/pop and enqueue/dequeue operations with labeled elements.

beats.narration: Apply Software Qualities: Cohesion & Minimal Coupling to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. Concepts of object- oriented design are a large part of the course. Consider this worked case: High cohesion means a class performs a single, well-defined purpose, while minimal coupling reduces dependencies between classes. On screen, display a before-and-after class diagram showing how refactoring improves cohesion and reduces coupling. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
beats.title: Software Qualities: Cohesion & Minimal Coupling
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a before-and-after class diagram showing how refactoring improves cohesion and reduces coupling.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Exception Handling & Control Flow, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. Exceptions interrupt normal control flow until a matching handler processes them or they propagate. Consider this worked case: A try-catch block catches a runtime error, allowing the program to recover or exit gracefully without crashing. On screen, show a control flow diagram with a normal path and an exception path branching to a handler block. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
beats.title: Exception Handling & Control Flow
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a control flow diagram with a normal path and an exception path branching to a handler block.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Compiler & IR Concepts with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Compiler work separates parsing and semantic analysis from lowering, verification, optimization, and target-specific code generation. Consider this worked case: LLVM IR serves as a typed, SSA-based intermediate representation that enables cross-platform optimization and code generation. On screen, illustrate a compiler pipeline diagram with stages: parsing, semantic analysis, lowering, verification, optimization, code generation. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.
beats.title: Compiler & IR Concepts
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a compiler pipeline diagram with stages: parsing, semantic analysis, lowering, verification, optimization, code generation.

beats.narration: Use Python Language Model & Execution to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Programs should be reasoned about through explicit state, control flow, data representation, contracts, tests, and observable behavior. Consider this worked case: Debugging separates syntax, runtime, and logical failures, while decomposition and abstraction reduce interacting concerns in Python code. On screen, show a Python object model diagram with identity, type, and value attributes, alongside a debugging workflow flowchart. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.
beats.title: Python Language Model & Execution
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a Python object model diagram with identity, type, and value attributes, alongside a debugging workflow flowchart.

beats.narration: Connect Object-Oriented Design Patterns to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. The course stresses problem solving while covering modern software development techniques and introducing essential software tools. Consider this worked case: The singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance, while the factory pattern creates objects without specifying exact classes. On screen, display a simple UML diagram of a factory pattern with creator, product, and concrete product classes. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
beats.title: Object-Oriented Design Patterns
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a simple UML diagram of a factory pattern with creator, product, and concrete product classes.

beats.narration: Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Valid IR must satisfy structural and typing rules. Consider this worked case: A checklist evaluates whether each class has a single responsibility, limited dependencies, and clear extension points for future features. On screen, show a printable checklist template with checkboxes for cohesion, coupling, modifiability, and extensibility evaluation. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a printable checklist template with checkboxes for cohesion, coupling, modifiability, and extensibility evaluation.

sources.excerpt: LLVM IR is a typed, SSA-based intermediate representation with explicit instructions, basic blocks, functions, memory operations, and control flow. A module contains global values, functions, declarations, and metadata. A function contains basic blocks, and every basic block ends with a terminator instruction. Phi instructions select values according to the predecessor control-flow edge. Load and store instructions make memory access explicit. Valid IR must satisfy structural and typing rules. The verifier reports IR that violates those rules. Compiler work separates parsing and semantic analysis from lowering, verification, optimization, and target-specific code generation.
